header: A number typed in a base (pure, no React): the typed line that opens the scientific calculator on a value in binary, octal, decimal or hexadecimal. I made the reader strict, so that no ordinary line is taken for it: a number with its own prefix: "0xFF", "0b1010", "0o17" (and "0xFF to decimal", "0b1010 in hex"); a number and where to write it: "255 to binary", "10 in hex", "1010 binary to decimal", "ff hex to octal". A number with no base word is decimal; the letters A-F are digits only when the number is said to be hexadecimal (a bare "ff" is not a number). Only whole numbers, up to 2^53 - 1 (the largest a float holds exactly): a longer number is not read, not rounded. I guess nothing: a digit the base does not have ("0b102", "19 binary to hex") is no number.
